title: Nước chấm
subtitle: Vietnamese garlic, lime and fish sauce dip, kept strong
intro:
> [!NOTE]
> **Draft method for David to check.** The vault note lists only the
> ingredients, so the method is worked out from them and hasn’t been tested.

This version has no water, so it is stronger than most: use it as is for
spooning over rice and grilled meat, or thin it for a dipping sauce (see
Notes). Dissolve the sugar fully before tasting.

steps.name: Dissolve the sugar
steps.markdown: Stir the sugar into the lime juice until it has dissolved. Warming the juice for a few seconds helps.

steps.name: Add the rest
steps.markdown: Stir in the fish sauce, garlic and chili garlic sauce.

steps.name: Taste and rest
steps.markdown: Taste for the balance of salty, sour and sweet, adding a little more lime or sugar if needed. Leave it for 10 minutes so the garlic flavours the sauce.

sections.title: Ingredients
sections.markdown:
- 4 tbsp [granulated sugar](/ingredients/sugar.md)
- 4 tbsp [lime juice](/ingredients/lime.md) (about 2 limes)
- 6 tbsp [fish sauce](/ingredients/fish-sauce.md)
- 6 cloves [garlic](/ingredients/garlic.md), minced
- 2 tsp [chili garlic sauce](/ingredients/chili-garlic-sauce.md)

sections.title: Method
sections.markdown:
1. **Dissolve the sugar.** Stir the sugar into the lime juice until it has dissolved. Warming the juice for a few seconds helps.
2. **Add the rest.** Stir in the fish sauce, garlic and chili garlic sauce.
3. **Taste and rest.** Taste for the balance of salty, sour and sweet, adding a little more lime or sugar if needed. Leave it for 10 minutes so the garlic flavours the sauce.

sections.title: Notes
sections.markdown:
- For a classic dipping sauce for spring rolls or bún, stir in 60–120 ml (¼–½ cup) warm water.
- Keeps for about a week in the fridge; the garlic gets stronger as it sits.
